detailed_rationale: Supreme Industries is India's largest plastic piping solutions provider (about 67% of revenue), offering 14,000+ SKUs of uPVC pipes and injection-moulded PVC fittings for plumbing, drainage and fire-protection applications, alongside a diversified set of smaller businesses -- cross-laminated films, protective packaging, moulded furniture and storage products, and composite LPG cylinders. The company is financially very strong: virtually debt-free (borrowings of only about Rs 91 crore as of March 2026 against a market cap of roughly Rs 44,800-44,850 crore), with ROCE of about 20.7% and a healthy 42.8% dividend payout ratio, consistent with the quant screen's very high quality_score (87.4) and near-zero D/E (0.015x) and very high interest coverage (53.6x). Growth has been steady rather than exceptional: TTM sales of about Rs 11,326 crore represent about 9% growth, close to the quant screen's revenue_growth_1y of 7.39%, with operating margin around 14-14.4%. The most recent reported quarter showed consolidated net profit up 38.76% YoY to about Rs 280.72 crore, a genuine recovery signal after a period in which the core piping segment faced 'unfavourable PVC resin prices and slower-than-expected demand recovery from infrastructure spending' during 9M FY25 -- a real, commodity-price-and-capex-timing headwind specific to plastic pipes (PVC resin is crude-oil-linked and its price swings directly compress or expand piping-segment margins) rather than a company-specific execution failure. The stock has de-rated substantially even as the underlying business kept growing and generating cash: down 13.5% over 1 year and a steep 39.0% over 2 years per the quant screen, reflecting a much richer multiple in the past that has partially normalized. Even after that de-rating, the valuation remains elevated on conventional yardsticks -- PE of about 43.4x and price-to-book of about 7.2x -- so this is a case of a very high-quality, financially pristine market leader whose price has come down from an even more demanding starting point rather than one that has become cheap.
recommendation_rationale: The quant screen carries this as Hold: an excellent quality score is weighed against a fair-to-moderate value score, consistent with a best-in-class, debt-free market leader that nonetheless still trades at a rich multiple even after a two-year de-rating. My own view agrees with Hold -- the business itself is genuinely high quality (market leadership, near-zero debt, steady dividend, resilient long-run demand for piping in India's housing/infrastructure build-out) and the latest quarter shows real recovery from the PVC-resin-price headwind, but at 43.4x trailing earnings and 7.2x book value there is limited room for multiple expansion, and the recent margin pressure from resin prices and infra-spending timing is a genuine, recurring cyclical risk for this specific segment. There's no basis to rescue this further and no analytical tension beyond ordinary commodity-input/capex-timing cyclicality that would warrant escalation -- a fair Hold on an excellent but richly-priced business.
summary: Supreme Industries is India's largest maker of plastic pipes and fittings, with a diversified set of smaller plastics businesses alongside its core piping franchise. The company is financially very strong -- virtually debt-free, with healthy returns on capital and a steady dividend -- and the most recent quarter showed a strong profit recovery after a period in which raw-material (PVC resin) price swings and slower government infrastructure spending had pressured the piping business. The stock has fallen meaningfully over the past one and two years even as the business kept growing, but remains richly valued on conventional measures. We rate it a Hold: an excellent, financially pristine market leader, but not yet a bargain even after the recent de-rating.
positive_para: A financially pristine, virtually debt-free market leader (67% of revenue from India's largest plastic-piping franchise, 14,000+ SKUs) with strong returns on capital (ROCE about 20.7%), a healthy 42.8% dividend payout, and a genuine recent recovery quarter (net profit up 38.76% YoY) after working through a PVC-resin-price and infrastructure-spending-timing headwind that pressured the core piping segment.
negative_para: The core piping segment's margins are directly exposed to PVC resin (crude-oil-linked) price swings and to the pace of government infrastructure spending, both outside the company's control, and this exact combination caused real segment margin compression through 9M FY25. Even after a 39% two-year share-price decline, the stock still trades at a rich 43.4x trailing earnings and 7.2x book value, leaving limited room for further multiple re-rating even as the underlying business recovers.
reverse_dcf_judgment: At about 43.4x trailing earnings and 7.2x book value for a business growing revenue at roughly high-single digits, the multiple still assumes a premium for quality and market leadership rather than pricing a bargain -- the two-year de-rating (-39%) brought the stock down from an even more demanding starting point, but did not make it cheap. The business quality (near-zero debt, strong ROCE, steady dividend) justifies some premium, but the PVC-resin and infra-spending-timing cyclicality means near-term growth can be lumpier than the multiple might suggest. Growth here is estimated well below the 25% hypergrowth band, so the ROE/dilution disclosure is not separately triggered.
technical_commentary: Supreme Industries topped in Jun-2024 at approximately Rs6056 and has printed two straight years of lower yearly highs since (Rs6056 to Rs4630 to Rs4024), now -42% off its ATH with a fully bearish monthly MA stack (price under the 10-, 20- and 40-month averages). No climax-volume flush is visible -- this looks like a grinding, unresolved Stage 4 decline rather than a capitulation low.
